domain_rule.milling_axis_policy: tool axis is fixed within one admitted three-axis milling operation; reorientation is an explicit non-cutting setup transition before a later operation
domain_rule.history: finite ordered manufacturing history with immutable source intent and explicit durable body/setup targets

stock.semantics: bounded regular volumetric material with explicit units, common workpiece frame and durable body identity
bounded closed/oriented imported material with explicit units, representation, durable body identity and source-uncertainty contract; import success alone is not validity

cutting_solid.semantics: finite external turning cutting region, including declared nose/profile geometry and a separately modelled non-cutting holder region
finite internal boring/turning cutting region with access and holder-clearance witness
finite grooving/parting cutting region capable of complete separation
finite formed cutting region; nonconvexity is permitted when physical access is witnessed
finite drill cutting solid usable in an admitted lathe or mill setup; machine family is a setup/kinematics fact, not encoded into the cutter identity
finite fixed-axis undercut/nonconvex cutting region with explicit access and non-cutting-body clearance witness

trajectory.semantics: finite-duration constant pose; an engaged stationary interval remains semantically present even when it causes no new removal
continuous finite line segment with explicit endpoints
continuous finite oriented planar arc with explicit endpoints, plane and sweep sense
continuous finite fixed-axis helical motion with explicit angular/axial progression; exact numeric encoding is owned by MC-003
finite ordered continuous composition of line segments
finite explicitly defined continuous curve; exact numeric representation is owned by MC-003
finite continuous composition of admitted trajectory pieces preserving semantic boundaries
finite motion retaining time/spindle-angle correlation where material sweep depends on phase

engagement.semantics: explicit finite interval with endpoint policy; only engaged intervals contribute cutting sweep
entry/exit is preserved as a semantic boundary even when geometrically tangent or redundant

lathe_kinematics.semantics: explicit workpiece rotation about a declared spindle axis with finite angle/time law
tool motion relative to the rotating target in the common workpiece frame
spindle/feed correlation retained rather than replaced by independent full-angle coverage
explicit noncoaxial workholding transform; full phase-sensitive sweep is required where rotational reduction is invalid

setup.semantics: explicit rigid transform between machine/setup and common workpiece frame
explicitly select a durable material body, establish new workholding and transform, then continue machining
explicit lathe↔mill transition preserving common-frame/body identities and immutable history

material.semantics: M_next = closure(interior(M \ S)); lower-dimensional debris may vanish, but positive-volume material may not be erased by policy
connectivity-changing removal creates an explicit durable body transition; no largest/primary-body discard rule
complete removal yields explicit empty material/body disappearance, not an invented residual
every machining operation names the durable target body/body set valid for that setup

witness_catalog.semantics: target body is supported/held by the current setup for the operation
commanded finite trajectory lies inside admitted machine travel/kinematic limits
cutting region can reach the target without relying on unmodelled impossible approach
declared non-cutting holder region does not pass through forbidden retained material/fixture on the witnessed route
internal tool/cutter has a physically admissible entry and clearance path
drill has an admissible axial approach for the selected setup
the operation's nominal material set changes volumetric connectivity as claimed
every subsequently machined separated body is retained by the current setup or explicitly re-clamped
finite spindle/tool correlation is explicitly specified where phase changes swept material
noncoaxial workholding transform is explicit in the common workpiece frame
non-cutting tool/holder and fixture clearance is explicitly witnessed
a durable material-body identity is selected without inferring identity from backend topology handles
new support/workholding is explicitly established after a re-clamp/re-chuck
setup-to-common-workpiece transform is explicit and rigid
each setup in a cross-machine history explicitly holds its target body
cross-machine/setup composition resolves into the versioned common workpiece frame
separated retained body is demonstrably held or explicitly re-clamped before further machining
operation or terminal transition identifies the affected durable body/body set

operation_map.boundary_semantics: may be exact no-new-removal; the canonical journal event remains
retrace/self-crossing/reversal/stationary segments remain ordinary finite inputs
empty material is a valid explicit terminal state

boundary_and_pathology_policy.policy: ordinary valid workload; exact/equality event handling remains a constructive obligation
ordinary valid workload; zero-volume contact cannot be promoted to a volumetric bridge and face contact requires local-interior analysis
ordinary nominal input; may not be collapsed to no-op solely by a tolerance threshold
ordinary material; regularization does not erase positive-volume remnants
ordinary finite trajectory semantics; immutable source intent is preserved even if no new material is removed
ordinary finite history; resource qualification belongs to MC-004/MC-046 and is not a domain exclusion
valid outcome when set reasoning/certificate establishes no new removed volume; commanded penetration into already-empty space does not become positive removal

named_domain_decisions.basis: MC-1 is lathe plus fixed-axis three-axis milling; explicit non-cutting setup reorientation is admitted, continuous cutting-time tool-axis reorientation is future scope rather than a provider refusal
current MC-1 is removal-focused lathe and mill; additive remains long-term product scope without being added to this tranche
geometry-critical nominal material is authoritative for MC-1; deformation, force and chip dynamics are not required for current engineering geometry

lathe and mill families are both in scope, but current contracts do not decide whether synchronized live-tool/driven-tool compound kinematics are one mandatory operation or an explicit machine/setup transition; provider limitations cannot decide this
single-spindle lathe plus explicit re-clamp/re-chuck histories are defined; multi-spindle transfer-machine semantics require explicit product intent before becoming mandatory constructors

coverage_rule.ordinary_operation_coverage: every currently required ordinary operation is admitted through explicit constructors; anything not yet fixed by product scope is represented by a named domain decision and may not be silently removed from the denominator

MC-005: integrate MC-002/003/004 and decide MC-A; MC-002 alone does not accept MC-A
MC-006_to_MC-008: constructive and finite-termination routes for every admitted constructor
MC-018_to_MC-023: actual cutter/tool sweep realization and setup composition
MC-054: engineering-output profile for singular/grouped material states
